newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds stable after profittaking, falls seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds stable after profittaking, falls seen.

text.p: Danish bond prices were only very slightly higher but stable on Thursday after a morning of profit-taking but dealers saw falls ahead.
"The market is becalmed up to the Christmas break with many players on holiday or closing their books. The profit-taking will probably continue, causing falls," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up a marginal 0.03 point from the opening at 108.94, recovering from earlier losses and yielding 6.66 percent in turnover of 700 million crowns while its March future rose 0.17 point to 108.03 with 175 contracts traded.

One dealer saw the 2006 benchmark falling as far down as 108.70 by the end of trading. The morning's Danish November CPI data - an unchanged 2.4 percent year-on-year rate - was expected by the market and had no affect on trade.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.10 point to 85.85.
The crown traded at 3.8258 per mark at 1225 gmt, down a smidgen from 3.8252 at the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 77 basis points from the start of trading.
